album.say: a new album · a photo album
ex: Do you like their new album?
I listen to this album every day.
The band has a new album.
Can I see your photo album?

talent.say: have a talent for · a talent show
ex: She has a talent for music.
Does your son have a talent for sports?
Our school has a talent show in May.
He has a real talent for drawing.
This candy costs fifty cents.
Is this pen fifty cents?
I have only ten cents.
There are a hundred cents in a dollar.
Can I talk to the management, please?
I study business management.
The new management is very good.
She works in hotel management.
Do you like the design of our website?
The new phone has a nice design.
She studies fashion design at college.
The design of this kitchen is very simple.

monster.say: afraid of monsters · a sea monster
ex: My son is afraid of monsters.
Is there a monster under my bed?
Let's watch a movie about a sea monster.
The kids drew a funny green monster.

email.say: send an email · email address · by email

progress.note: Uncountable: good progress, a lot of progress (not "a progress").
ex: You are making good progress in English.
The doctor is happy with my progress.
We made a lot of progress today.
Is there any progress with my visa?

visit.say: pay a visit · a visit to the doctor · on a visit
visit.note: Most often "visit" is a verb: "Come and visit us!"
ex: Thanks for your visit!
Is this your first visit to Kyiv?
My parents came for a short visit.
How much is a visit to the doctor?

cop.note: Informal. The neutral word is "police officer."
ex: A cop asked to see my license.
Please call the cops now!
Her brother is a cop.
Ask that cop for directions.

community.say: the online community · in the community
community.note: Most often "community" means the people in one area: "Our community has a new park."
ex: The online community helped me fix my phone.
Is there an online community for this game?
I am in a big photo community online.
Our IT community meets every Friday.

bro.note: Very informal slang. Use only with close friends.
ex: Thanks a lot, bro!
Can you help me, bro?
Hey bro, how are you?
See you tomorrow, bro.

mayor.say: the mayor of · a new mayor

ex: She is the national tennis champion.
Who is the world champion now?
Our team is the city champion this year.
The champion gets a big gold cup.

signal.say: no signal · a weak signal · lose the signal

limit.say: speed limit · time limit · over the limit
limit.note: Also a common verb, to limit: "Limit your time on the phone."

bullshit.note: Vulgar; don't use it at work or with strangers. Polite word: "nonsense."
ex: That's bullshit, and you know it.
I don't believe his bullshit.
Is this story true or bullshit?
This ad is total bullshit.
Water is an important natural resource.
This website is a great resource for students.
Can you share some good resources for learning English?
We need more resources to finish the project.

media.say: in the media · on social media
media.note: Often with "the": "in the media." Also "social media": "on social media."

mama.note: Informal or childish; "mom" is more common in American English.

click.say: with one click · a mouse click
click.note: Most often "click" is a verb: "Click the button."
ex: One click and the file is open.
Buy this with just one click.
The site counts every click.
Can I pay with one click here?

shopping.say: go shopping · do the shopping · a shopping center
shopping.note: Uncountable. Say "go shopping" or "do the shopping."

website.say: on the website · visit a website
ex: Please visit our website for more information.
What is the website address?
I buy tickets on the website.
The website does not work today.

credit.say: on credit · credit card · a loan (not a credit)
credit.note: Not "a credit" for money from a bank: say "a loan." Use "on credit," "credit card."
ex: We bought the car on credit.
Can I buy this phone on credit?
Can I pay by credit card here?
Bad credit makes it hard to get a loan.

incident.say: report an incident · an incident on the bus
incident.note: Formal word. In everyday talk, people often say "something happened."
ex: There was an incident on the bus today.
Please report any incident to the manager.
Nobody was hurt in the incident.
Can you tell me about the incident?

clerk.say: a bank clerk · an office clerk
clerk.note: In the US, a "clerk" is also a person who works in a store or at a hotel desk.
ex: She works as a clerk in a bank.
Ask the clerk for the form.
The clerk checks all the papers.
Is the clerk in the office today?

candidate.say: a candidate for · vote for a candidate

account.say: log in to your account · create an account
account.note: Most often "account" means a bank account: "Put the money in my account."

theater.say: go to the theater · at the theater
theater.note: British spelling: theatre. A "movie theater" is a place to watch movies.
ex: We went to the theater on Saturday.
Is the theater next to the park?
I love the theater more than movies.
Let's buy theater tickets for Friday.

author.say: the author of · a favorite author

drink.say: have a drink · go out for a drink · buy someone a drink
drink.note: Most often "drink" is a verb: "I drink tea." A drink can be any drink, like juice.
ex: Let's go out for a drink after work.
Can I buy you a drink?
She ordered a drink at the bar.
I only have one drink at parties.

bar.say: at a bar · go to a bar
bar.note: Also a long piece of something: "a chocolate bar," "a bar of soap."

cousin.say: my cousin · on my mom's side
cousin.note: Used for both male and female cousins.
ex: My cousin lives in Kyiv.
Do you have any cousins?
I have ten cousins on my mom's side.
We visit our cousins every summer.

senator.say: a state senator · vote for a senator
ex: The senator answered our questions.
Who is the senator from your state?
We wrote a letter to our senator.
The senator visited our school.

region.say: in the region · a region of the country

fashion.say: in fashion · out of fashion · a fashion show
ex: She loves fashion and new clothes.
Are long coats in fashion this year?
He works in the fashion business.
I don't follow fashion.

concept.say: the concept of · a new concept

inspector.say: a health inspector · a building inspector
ex: The health inspector visits the restaurant every year.
Is the inspector coming today?
The inspector checked the building for safety.
A police inspector came to the house.

reporter.say: a TV reporter · a news reporter
ex: She works as a TV reporter.
A reporter asked me some questions.
Is he a reporter for the local paper?
He wants to be a sports reporter.

festival.say: at the festival · a music festival · a film festival
ex: We went to a music festival last summer.
The town has a food festival in May.
When does the festival start?
Tickets for the festival are sold out.

jury.say: on the jury · the jury chose
jury.note: Most often "jury" means the people who decide a case in court: "The jury said he is guilty."
ex: The jury liked her song best.
Who is on the jury this year?
She was on the jury at the film festival.
The jury gave him first place.

concert.say: go to a concert · at the concert

alcohol.note: Uncountable: some alcohol, no alcohol (not "an alcohol").
ex: I don't drink alcohol.
No alcohol is allowed in the park.
Does this drink have alcohol?
Alcohol is bad for your health.

budget.say: on a budget · a tight budget · over budget

pizza.say: order a pizza · a slice of pizza

madam.say: excuse me, madam · Dear Sir or Madam
madam.note: Formal; "ma'am" is more common in American speech.
ex: Excuse me, madam, can I help you?
This way, please, madam.
Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to you.
Good evening, madam. Your table is ready.

sexy.note: Informal; can sound rude when said about someone you don't know well.
ex: She looks sexy in that red dress.
Do you think this dress is too sexy?
The singer has a sexy voice.
He thinks his new car is sexy.

sport.say: play a sport · do sports · favorite sport
sport.note: Americans usually say "sports": "Do you like sports?"

tiger.say: a tiger at the zoo · a white tiger
ex: We saw a tiger at the zoo.
Can we go and see the tigers?
The tiger is sleeping in the sun.
My son drew a tiger at school.

rice.note: Uncountable: some rice, not "a rice" or "rices".

palace.say: a royal palace · visit a palace

telephone.say: on the telephone · answer the telephone · telephone number
telephone.note: In everyday speech people usually just say "phone".

visitor.say: have visitors · visitors to the museum
ex: We had visitors last weekend.
Visitors can park here for free.
The museum gets many visitors in summer.
Are visitors allowed in the hospital today?

farmer.say: a local farmer · a farmers' market
ex: The farmer sells eggs at the market.
My grandfather was a farmer.
Do you buy milk from a local farmer?
Farmers work very hard.

post.say: write a post · like a post · in a post
post.note: Most often "post" is a verb: "Post a photo." In British English, "post" also means mail.

factor.say: a big factor · the main factor · a factor in
ex: Price is an important factor for me.
Weather is a big factor in our plans.
What is the main factor in your choice?
Stress is a factor in many illnesses.

alarm.say: fire alarm · car alarm · set the alarm
alarm.note: Also an alarm clock: "Set the alarm for seven."
ex: The fire alarm is very loud.
Can you stop the alarm, please?
Our car has an alarm.
Is that the fire alarm ringing?

match.say: watch a match · win a match · a tennis match
match.note: Most often a verb: "The shoes match the bag." In the US, "game" is common for team sports.
